meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'May love be your guide in every moment of your life'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Paulo Coelho everywhere, but sourced to nothing. Wikiquote lists it as misattributed. The honest verdict.

answer.label: Not verified as Paulo Coelho — an unsourced internet attribution
answer.sourceLine: This exact line is not found in any of Paulo Coelho’s published works. English Wikiquote lists it under Misattributed, noting the phrasing was “widely attributed to Coelho on the internet” but “has not been located in any editions available in online searches.” The underlying sentiment — “let love be your guide” — is an old, generic directive that predates Coelho. No book, page, interview, or letter has ever been produced for the specific wording.

source.excerpt: May love be your guide in every moment of your life
trail: English Wikiquote places this line in its Misattributed section, noting it was “widely attributed to Coelho on the internet” but “has not been located in any editions available in online searches.”
Aggregator pages such as Quotefancy reproduce the line with a portrait and no citation — no book title, no page, no date.
Wikiquote observes that the directive “Let love be your guide” is “a very old one, and did not originate with Coelho,” so even the sentiment is not distinctively his.
Quote Investigator has no entry for this line — it has not surfaced in any documented Coelho text to investigate.
source.excerptNote: The line appears almost exclusively on quotation-aggregator sites (Quotefancy, AZQuotes, BrainyQuote, Goodreads) with no book, chapter, or page attached.
source.rightsNote: Because the exact wording cannot be tied to any identifiable work or first publication, no copyright status can be asserted. author.name: Paulo Coelho
author.heading: About the name it gets pinned to
author.metaLine: b. 24 August 1947 · Brazilian novelist · author of The Alchemist
author.bio: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian lyricist and novelist, best known for The Alchemist (1988), one of the best-selling books in history. His aphoristic, spiritual style makes him one of the internet’s most common magnets for feel-good lines — many circulated in his name were never written by him. This is one such orphaned quotation: consistent in tone with his work, but absent from it.

misattribution.heading: How this became a “Coelho quote”
misattribution.intro: The line rides Paulo Coelho’s name across social media and quote sites, but no one has ever produced the book it supposedly comes from.

items.why: English Wikiquote files this line under Misattributed, explaining it was “widely attributed to Coelho on the internet” and “originally added here within the section for The Alchemist,” but “this specific form has not been located in any editions available in online searches.”
Wikiquote notes that the directive “Let love be your guide” is “a very old one, and did not originate with Coelho” — so even the idea is not his invention.

misattribution.truthLine: There is no documented Coelho source for this sentence. It is best described as an unsourced attribution — a warm, generic aphorism attached to a famous name.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Coelho
lead: Paulo Coelho’s public voice — short, hopeful, faintly mystical — is easy to imitate, and his enormous fame makes his name a convenient label for any uplifting line. That combination is exactly what produces “orphan quotes”: sentences that sound like an author until you go looking for the page they came from and find nothing.

The honest position here is not “fake” in the sense of maliciously invented, but unsourced: widely repeated, tonally plausible, and yet unlocated in the actual body of Coelho’s writing. Until someone cites a specific book, chapter, or interview, it cannot be called his.
context.pull: Sounds like Coelho. Sourced to nothing.
